product.reading: Reading what each database is doing.

tls.verify: Verify the certificate and the name (recommended)

plan.estimated: Estimated by the planner: EXPLAIN without ANALYZE plans the statement and does not run it.
plan.generic_one: A generic plan, made without the value of its parameter. Estimated by the planner; nothing was run.
plan.generic_other: A generic plan, made without the values of its {{count}} parameters. Estimated by the planner; nothing was run.

overviewPage.description_one: {{count}} instance, sampled every {{seconds}} s from its statistics views.
overviewPage.description_other: {{count}} instances, each sampled every {{seconds}} s from its statistics views.
overviewPage.warnings: {{name}}: what its monitoring role should change
overviewPage.noSamplesDetail: The first comes within {{seconds}} seconds; a chart needs two.
overviewPage.waitEventsDetail: {{name}}, the last hour: what active sessions waited on

welcomePage.description: Database reads PostgreSQL's own statistics with a monitoring role, and changes nothing.
welcomePage.step1: On each PostgreSQL server, create a role that is only in pg_monitor, and load pg_stat_statements. Setup has the statements.
welcomePage.step2: Add the server under Instances with that role. Its password is sealed with this install's key and never shown again.
welcomePage.step3: Within a minute the first sample is in; queries show from the second.

queriesPage.description_one: {{count}} statement ran in the range, grouped by its normalized text.
queriesPage.description_other: {{count}} statements ran in the range, grouped by their normalized text.
queriesPage.notYet: Queries show from the second sample, once there is a difference to count.

topDetail.1: By total time, the last hour
topDetail.24: By total time, the last 24 hours
topDetail.168: By total time, the last 7 days

locksPage.description: Who blocks whom, right now: chains from pg_blocking_pids(), read every 5 seconds. Each starts at the session the others wait behind.
locksPage.idleTitle: {{who}} has been in a transaction for {{time}} and is doing nothing
locksPage.idleDetail: Its transaction holds its locks until it commits or rolls back. Find the application that opened it; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout ends such sessions on its own.
locksPage.chainsDetail: The sessions with the most waiting behind them first
locksPage.none: No session waits on a lock
locksPage.unseen: A session the monitoring role cannot see

replicationPage.description: Standbys, how far behind they are, and replication slots, read from the instance every 15 seconds.
replicationPage.staleTitle: The inactive slot {{name}} keeps {{size}} of WAL
replicationPage.staleDetail: Nothing reads from it, and the server keeps its WAL until it advances, so the disk fills. If its consumer is gone, a DBA can drop it with pg_drop_replication_slot(); Database changes nothing.
replicationPage.noStandbys: No standby streams from this instance

connectionsPage.description: {{used}} client connections of {{max}}, from pg_stat_activity, read every 10 seconds.

explainPage.description: The plan of a statement, and where its cost is. It is planned in a read-only transaction and never run: EXPLAIN, without ANALYZE.
explainPage.sqlHint: One SELECT, WITH, VALUES, TABLE, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE. $1, $2 as in Queries are fine: the plan is then the generic one.
explainPage.editorsOnlyDetail: Explain sends a statement to the database to be planned, so it needs the editor role.
explainPage.notRun: Explain a statement to see its plan

instancesPage.description: The PostgreSQL servers Database watches, and the monitoring role it signs in with.
instancesPage.addDetail: PostgreSQL 14 or newer, reached directly rather than through a pooler. Database signs in as a role that is only in pg_monitor; every session it opens is read-only.
instancesPage.name: Name
instancesPage.passwordHint: Sealed with this install's key and never shown again.
instancesPage.passwordKeep: Leave it empty to keep the one saved; it is never shown.
instancesPage.plainTitle: The password and every statistic go over the network in the clear
instancesPage.plainDetail: Only for a server on the same host or a network nobody else is on. Otherwise turn on ssl in postgresql.conf and verify its certificate.
instancesPage.caHint: The PEM certificate the server's certificate is signed with, when it is not one this system trusts. Leave it empty otherwise.
instancesPage.noneDetail: An admin adds the first one; Setup has the role to create for it.
instancesPage.confirmDelete: Delete {{name}} and everything sampled of it? Its database is not touched.

setupPage.description: What to do on each PostgreSQL server once, before adding it.
setupPage.roleDetail: pg_monitor reads the statistics views and every session's query, and can change nothing. pg_stat_statements groups queries by their normalized text.
setupPage.explainDetail: Planning a statement needs the right to read the tables it names. Grant it only for the schemas you want to explain; without it Explain answers permission denied and the rest works.
setupPage.hba: Who may sign in as it
setupPage.hbaDetail: Let the role in only from Database's address, over TLS.
setupPage.prometheusDetail: /metrics has each instance's last sample: up, connections, sessions waiting on a lock or idle in a transaction, lag, transactions and cache hits.

settingsPage.askAnAdmin: Ask an admin of this Database.

account.title: Account
account.description: Your profile, password, two-step verification and where you are signed in.

members.title: Members
members.description: Who can sign in to this Database, and with which role. Viewers see everything; editors also check instances and explain statements; admins also add and change instances, and manage members and tokens.

signin.title: Sign-in
signin.description: Identity providers people can sign in with, such as OpenAsy Identity, Keycloak or Microsoft Entra ID, and which of their groups give which role.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.description: For scripts and CI. Each token has one role and an expiry; the secret is shown once.
